content.thinking:
I should write the whole module carefully in one pass without testing, designing a Warcraft-style ancient treant around 5 meters tall. I'm planning the skeleton structure starting with hips as root, then spine segments, chest, neck, and head, keeping to well-understood API calls to avoid errors.

Now I'm sketching the full skeleton: jaw, arms with shoulder-elbow-wrist-finger chains like root branches, legs with thigh-knee-ankle-foot and root-toe details, plus a crown of branches holding leaf cards, moss, glowing eyes, and a few rune glows -- rich but manageable. I'm defining the coordinate convention (model faces +Z, right is +X) and settling on a bark/moss/leaf color palette with amber glowing eyes and teal-green glowing runes before laying out the actual joint positions for the spine chain.

Now I'm continuing the skeleton build: adding a neck chain running from the chest up through two neck joints to the head, positioning the head near the top of a roughly 5.5-5.6m tall figure, and starting to block out the hips and thick trunk-like legs to match a chunky Blizzard-style treant proportion with an oversized head and arms and short legs.

Setting head direction forward-up, then placing the jaw joint off the head aimed slightly down and forward. For the torso body, considering sweeping along the spine chain to create the loft geometry.

Laying out torso stations with increasing width and depth going up the spine, then adding shoulder burls as spheres attached to the chest bone, and starting to sketch the arm chains sprouting from shoulder joints.

For the arms, I'm going with a slightly angled, extended pose rather than full T-pose for a more natural readable silhouette — defining shoulder, elbow, wrist, and hand positions as a joint chain mirrored for left/right sides.

Still defining arm radii and chains...

Now I'm designing the hand as a gnarled palm with four finger digits branching from the wrist joint, each finger a short two-segment chain curling downward with spread across X, parented to the hand tip.

Working out finger and thumb geometry...

Now moving to the legs: hips at either side, with knee bend forward and foot targets set, computing limb lengths against hip-to-foot distances to keep joints consistent.

Still planning foot anatomy...

Now shifting to the head: a chunky skull sphere around 1.2 wide, positioned near the top, with a brow ridge, a wedge-like nose, and a jaw joint for the mouth.

For the treant's face I want wooden mouth parts, a mossy beard made of hanging moss cards and vines, and glowing amber eye spheres set deep under the brow. The crown rises from the head as antler-like branches topped with a leafy canopy -- clusters of leaf cards and low-poly icosahedron foliage blobs for that chunky Warcraft look, built as branch chains sprouting from the head joint.

I'm planning five crown branches plus shoulder and back branches, each with a sweep geometry and leaf clumps at the tips, using SVG leaf textures in green and autumn-gold tones that I can tint via color multiplication. I'm now writing a helper function that scatters leaf cards into bursts around a center point using random directions on a sphere.

For bark, I'm composing a custom paint function layered from a wood-grain pattern with moss patches appearing on upward-facing surfaces based on noise thresholds.

Still refining the texture blend...

Adding moss patches via noise thresholds on the upper surfaces, plus thin crack-like veins using cell distance differences for painted amber sap and dark crevices. Performance should be fine since paints evaluate per texel, and I'll want separate darker paint variants for the legs.

For texel density, I'm estimating about 60 square meters of painted surface across torso, legs, and arms, which suggests bumping paint resolution to 2048 to keep detail crisp while reserving flat colors for smaller elements to conserve sheet space. For chest burls, I'm thinking of scattering small icosahedron bumps along sticks, using flat bark-toned colors rather than painted textures to save area.

Now I'm considering adding a glowing rune decal on the chest, using a surface ray cast to find a precise point on the torso front and applying a glow effect to the decal part, though I'm weighing the risk of the ray returning null.

For the eyes, I'm planning small glowing spheres with dark pupil boxes recessed under slanted brow ridges, built from simple sphere and box geometries attached to the head bone. I'm sketching out the head's basic shape starting with a skull sphere at the head's center point.

Still working out the facial geometry...

I'm calculating where the skull's curved surface sits at the eye's x-position so I can place the eye sockets flush against it, landing eyes around z=1.12 with slight protrusion for the eyeballs themselves, then checking where the muzzle should begin relative to the skull's front edge.

Now I'm working out jaw mechanics - the lower jaw as a frustum shape hinging at a joint point, an upper lip frustum, a dark interior for the mouth cavity, and small tusk-like cone teeth jutting up from the lower jaw in an ivory bone color for that Warcraft aesthetic.

Thinking about overall scale: the head sits around 1.24 wide and 1.2 tall, with crown branches reaching toward 6 meters total height for this ancient treant.

For the beard, I'm planning Spanish moss hanging from the jaw and cheeks using upward-facing card frames with a tendril-drawn moss texture, plus thicker root-like beard sweeps curving down from the chin using catmull curves with tapering radius.

Now I'm designing a reusable branch-building function for the crown's antler-like limbs -- it builds a chain from a catmull-spline path, sweeps bark-colored geometry along it, and caps the tip with a leaf cluster, while also planning smaller side twigs branching off the main limbs at intermediate points.

For bone budgeting I'm roughly tallying joint counts across spine, limbs, fingers, toes, and crown branches to stay safely under the 160-joint limit, then planning icosahedron-based leaf clumps in a few varied colors to scatter across the branch tips.

Each branch roughly adds up to around ten parts with sweeps, twigs, icosahedron clumps, and leaf cards, so across nine branches the whole thing stays manageable at a few hundred parts and roughly eight to ten thousand triangles total. I'm also sketching in mossy shoulder pauldrons with tiny sapling trees growing out of them for a whimsical touch.

Now I'm adding small decorative fungi -- mushroom caps on lathe geometry with white-spotted decals, plus flat shelf fungus discs along the torso sides using simple flattened cylinder shapes in warm orange and cream tones. I'm also considering subtle fantasy flourishes like a woven vine belt with a golden ring buckle to give the treant a bit of a Warcraft-inspired silhouette.

I'm thinking through accessories that still feel natural for a treant -- a twisted vine rope belt with a golden acorn pendant, bark-and-ivy bracers, and a hanging amulet with a glowing core. I'm checking whether the torso's loft surface actually extends far enough down to support a loop sweep at hip height, since the round cap geometry might only reach partway before the separate leg meshes begin, and I need to confirm how the hip joint's orientation inherits from its parent to properly place that belt loop.

For the buckle, I'll cast a ray forward to find the torso surface hit point and orient the piece along the normal there. Still working out the loft path's normal direction convention for consistency.

I'm sketching the back details with bark plates and saplings filtered by surface normal, then planning the hip region by adding a wider pelvis station to anchor the torso spine chain before the legs.

For the arm attachment, I'm checking that the shoulder joint sits inside the chest width and placing a burl sphere near the shoulder bone to cover the junction cleanly.

Now I'm adding ancientness with hanging moss on the arms—scattering small clump-of-blades moss cards on upward-facing surfaces of the arm sweeps, filtering by normal direction so they only appear on top faces, with around 40 cards per arm using a tuft texture.

I'm settling on tuft counts: 120 on the torso, 30 per arm, 25 per leg, plus some on the shoulders, then starting to carefully write the typed code with correct imports—THREE, the builder, skeleton types, paint helpers, texture and glow utilities—making sure I only import what's actually used so I don't trigger unused-import errors.

Setting up the module imports and type definitions...

Now I'm defining the metadata for the model (name, style, commit reference) and laying out a bark-and-moss color palette with layered dark-to-light tones for the trunk, crevices, and seasonal leaf variations.

Writing bark texture logic...

Adding moss coloring with noise variation...

Reusing the leg and head paint, defining a dark mouth color, and building an SVG leaf texture with layered green shapes and vein details...

Writing more texture SVGs...

I'm designing a rune texture with a glowing circle sigil containing a tree glyph, then moving on to building the treant's skeleton structure starting with a hip joint and spine chain.

Still building skeleton joints...

Then I'm setting up the torso loft geometry bound to the spine chain, checking whether the sweep options correctly accept a bone/chain parameter.

Now I'm working out the neck sweep radii and attaching the head's skull sphere and cheek burl geometry to the head bone with appropriate scale and position offsets.

Still writing head details... ear knots as branch stubs, brow as a capsule between two points, and the start of a catmull-rom sweep for the nose root.

Now I'm positioning the mouth: an upper lip box, figuring out jaw joint placement relative to the skull bottom, and setting coordinates so the lower jaw box aligns properly beneath it.

I'm placing the upper lip and lower jaw boxes with a small gap between them for the mouth, setting the jaw joint position, and adding tusk spikes jutting from the lower jaw with options for bone attachment and color.

I'm checking that the skull fits properly over the neck geometry so the head connects without gaps, then starting to plan the crown branches growing from the top of the head, laying out the first vertical branch path with slightly offset points rising upward.

Still defining crown branches...

Now I'm sketching a branch helper function that builds a catmull-rom chain from points, attaches it to a parent joint with named sub-joints, and sweeps a bark-textured tube along it with a tapering radius—keeping the shoulder and back branches bound to the chest joint.

Building twigs along each branch joint with randomized outward directions and spike shapes, then adding small leaf clumps at the twig tips via a foliage function.

Still configuring card parameters...

Working out arm construction with chain joints along catmull-rom points for shoulder, elbow, wrist, and hand, parented to the chest -- though I'm reconsidering whether the curve should pass straight through the knot positions rather than smoothing them.

Now I'm setting up the sweep radii for arm thickness tapering toward the wrist, then attaching a palm sphere to the arm's tip joint, and working out finger base offsets so each digit curls forward and down with a slight splay from the hand center.

Still writing joint positions...

Still writing vine and cuff geometry...

Now moving to the leg construction: I'll set hip and foot points, then use a limb function returning root, knee, and end vectors with appropriate bend lengths to keep the knee flexing forward naturally.

Settling on leg radii tapering from hip to ankle, with a knee burl sphere and a rounded ankle cap that dips slightly below the path's end for a natural joint bulge. Now sketching the foot as a wide wooden sphere shape positioned at the base.

Working out toe chains as small polylines branching from the foot front, each swept with tapering radii and dark claw cones at the tips, then moving into the root flares spreading out from the base.

Still placing root paths...

Chest plates scattered as small bark-colored boxes across the torso, oriented along surface normals with random spin, plus knot bumps as stuck spheres and a glowing rune decal with amber heart-crack details on the chest.

Now I'm adding glowing amber vein tubes radiating from the rune outward across the torso surface, draping rough point paths onto the nearest front-facing surface and sweeping thin glowing tubes along them, mirrored for both sides of the chest.

For the back, I'm planning small sapling details near the upper shoulder blades, using raycasts against the torso skin to find attachment points and handling cases where the ray might miss.

Sapling placement needs a spike for the trunk and foliage offset along the surface normal, falling back to a default bone if the hit doesn't return one. Then I'm scattering shelf mushrooms along the torso sides and back by filtering hits where the normal points mostly sideways...

Actually, rethinking the mushroom shape — I'll go with a classic toadstool instead: a thin stem stuck into upward-facing surfaces (normal.y > 0.6, like shoulders or arms) with a rounded hemisphere cap positioned just above the stem, so they sit upright regardless of exact surface orientation.

I'm also planning to scatter small clusters of them across shoulder burls and the head using surface placement, maybe five per cluster.

For the mossy bits, I'm figuring out hanging frames along the jaw line, brow, and under the shoulder burls, giving them an upward lean and flow direction so they drape naturally.

I'm sketching a generic hang helper that takes points, bone, and size params, builds frames facing up, and scatters moss cards with some spin variance so they look natural from multiple angles. I'm also considering adding small decorative touches to the crown—maybe tiny flowers or golden acorn-like leaves for warmth.

Now I'm working out the chin beard using swept root paths: looping through a handful of strands with slightly offset x positions, defining start/mid/end points that taper down from the jaw toward the chest, with a dark bark-brown color and radius tapering to a point. I'm using Catmull-Rom curves bound explicitly to the jaw bone, checking that the beard ends roughly align with the chest position.

I confirm the beard sits cleanly in front of the chest without clipping, and decide to skip extra details like moss hair crowns or ear ornaments. For foliage, I'm planning branch clumps with leaf cards and small icosahedron accents, keeping the triangle count reasonable across all cards, and deciding the ground doesn't need extra geometry since the feet already root into it. Now I'm considering adding a hanging leaf skirt around the hips, using an "along" helper to distribute leaf frames around a belt loop.

Writing skirt leaf frames...

For the eyes, I'm positioning a glowing amber sphere on the head bone, adding a small dark slit pupil and a darker eye socket shape behind it to give it depth. Then I'm thinking about adding moss tufts for eyebrows along the brow capsule using sweep frames for placement.

I'll keep the antlers and ears as they are, then consider adding a small glowing amber acorn pendant on a vine necklace around the neck as a chest decoration, though I'm weighing whether that's worth the complexity.

Actually, I'll scrap the amulet idea since it'd overlap with the beard, and instead place the rune decal lower on the chest where it won't conflict. For the decal placement, I'm computing the hit point and surface normal on the torso to orient the rune correctly, then applying a glow effect to that part since decals return a regular part that supports glowing. I'm also refining the spine chain stations for the torso loft, nudging the z-offsets forward slightly at each height to give the torso a more natural curve.

Now I'm working through the cap geometry at the top of the torso loft -- worried the rounded end cap might balloon up too far and poke into the head/neck area. I'm considering using a flat cap at the top instead so it reads as a plateau that gets covered by the shoulder burls, rather than a dome that looks like an awkward hump, and adjusting the final station's width down to keep the end cap smaller and better contained.

I'm also reworking the bottom end cap -- the first station was too low, creating a weird belly-sack shape dangling between the legs near the crotch, so I'm shifting the starting station higher and adjusting its width/height so the dome sits more naturally as the trunk's base, and resequencing the stations upward (1.85, 2.4, 3.0, 3.55, 3.95) to keep everything proportioned. I confirm the belt placement between stations works fine, and note fingers, shoulder attachment, and facial knot counts are all fine too.

Writing SVG code...

Writing SVG rune circles...

I'm checking that the rune's root lines stay within the circle bounds, adjusting endpoints so they don't overshoot, then setting up a flat color palette for foliage leaves.

Now I'm writing helper functions for vector math and a foliage generator that scatters small icosahedron shapes as leaf clusters around each branch tip, picking random colors from the palette with occasional gold accents...

Still working out leaf texture lists and scaling card sizes relative to radius...

Setting rigid bone properties, importing the Joint type from the skeleton module, and planning out arm tip chains and bark color fills before writing the head and cheek geometry parts.

Now I'm starting to write the actual build function file, setting up the builder with a paint size and random seed, then defining a branch helper that creates chains from control points with radius, leaf size, and twig parameters...

Writing branch helper code...

Checking the index bounds for the joint array against point counts to make sure the twig loop doesn't run out of range for smaller chains.

The sweep function takes the radius array as its second argument with the bark color as options, and branch tips get rounded caps for the foliage. I'm setting up the crown chain's parent-child relationship with the head and chest joints, and considering whether back branches and hair foliage should also sprout from the chest.

I'm writing a helper to generate hanging moss cards positioned along bones with configurable size, lean, and spin, using a sink value to pull the card root back along its starting direction. I'm placing the hanging moss points along the lower edge of the shoulder burl, tracing an arc just below its surface.

Now I'm deciding against hanging moss from the elbows and going with simple tufts instead, adding elbow burl spheres bound to the elbow joint. For surface tufts on the torso, I'm scattering small crossed cards filtered to upward-facing normals with minimum spacing, and planning to do the same for the head.

For mushroom growths, I'm writing a helper that scatters points on a target surface with upward-facing filters, then sticks a tapered cylinder stem to each hit's bone (falling back to a default joint if none exists) and caps it with a hemisphere dome in alternating colors, varying stem thickness and cap size per-instance using the loop index.

Then I'm placing small spot decorations on the mushroom caps and double-checking I'm staying under my 64-color palette budget by listing out which bark, leaf, and metallic tones I've actually used versus declared.

Now I'm figuring out where to add bronze/gold trim bands on the limbs—cuffs at wrists and ankles—computing the positions by lerping between joint points along the leg sweep to place a band partway up the shin.

Similarly for arms, I'm placing a cuff band around the forearm near the wrist, plus a second thicker mossy green band higher up near the shoulder.

Now I'm adding bronze sweep bands with gold rivets spaced along the loop, using frame-based positioning so each rivet inherits the correct bone weighting automatically.

I'll create a reusable band helper so the same logic works for both the bronze band and a vine belt — generating a second lifted loop for rivets to sit flush on the surface, and reusing the helper with twisted vine geometry plus a buckle, skipping rivets for that variant.

For the belt skirt I'm sampling a lower-hip loop into 24 points, framing each sample along the loop direction, and layering two rows of leaf cards (gold and leaf-colored) hanging down to cover the pelvis area between the hips and upper thighs.

I'm checking that each loop plane I query actually intersects the torso geometry at the right heights (around y=2.1 for the torso ring, y=3.1 for rune decals) so the sampling doesn't throw errors, then drawing a sap-vein drape with a closed catmull curve swept as a thin glowing tube.

Now I'm building the brow geometry: creating a capsule-based sweep for each brow, then placing tuft cards along several points on that sweep with leaning and sizing...

Still writing limb details... I'm adding thorn spikes at the elbows and knees (angled outward and forward respectively), setting up the full limb-building code with typed point arrays and sweep radius profiles, and looping over left/right sides to generate matching chains with proper naming.

Now I'm connecting legs to the hip joints and fingers to the arm tips, double-checking that all imports and types are actually used so the compiler stays happy, and making sure unused function parameters won't trigger a strict lint error.

Writing scatter details for sticks and burls...

Moving to the beard and finalizing the return of the root object, making sure card colors default properly and textured surfaces keep their own hues. I'm also setting up a decal hit test by raycasting onto the torso surface to place a glowing decal, then starting on sap vein drapes.

Still figuring vine placement...

Now I'm checking frustumBox orientation defaults for the head geometry.

Moving on to the chin and beard details now.
